description: Ex US Navy Bu122120 c/n D.804. Acquired 1993, restored by Grumman in the USA from December 1994 and returned to Thailand (U-Tapao) May 2003; flew again February 2007 fitted with a C-123 engine. Moved to the Tango Don Mueang museum 10 December 2007; survived the November 2011 floods in place. Marked 120 with code 1234.

Ex RAF PS836; 836 also noted on a panel. Awaiting rebuild at Chiang Mai in 1980, at the RTAF workshops at Bang Sue in 1986 and in the Thai Airways workshops at Don Mueang from 1995; to the Tango Don Mueang museum by August 2002. Displayed in green primer.
Ex USAF 57-0538; noted in the 904 Squadron hangar at Don Mueang in 1995-97 and in the Tango Don Mueang museum from August 2002. Marked 1133 and 40-31.
T-28D-5, probably ex USAF 51-3534; displayed marked O-13534 with code 5306. Restored by Thai Airways November 1992; at Tango Don Mueang since February 2004.

Replica of the North American P-64 rebuilt in the USA from AT-6 airframe 88-12956 / Bu27560 by Carl Schmieder; certificated October 1990, bought by the Foundation for the Preservation and Development of Thai Aircraft in 1994 and exported to Thailand 12 August 1997. Marked 4300 and named Hanuman.
Ex Royal Thai Survey Department Aero Commander 690, c/n 11340; static in the Tango Don Mueang museum since August 2002.
Probably ex USAF 51-5044. Stored at Prachuap Khiri Khan 2000-2003, at Klong 15 2010-2013 and at the Tango Don Mueang museum since mid-2013. Wears 5044 and code 53154.

Ex USAF 51-7322. Restored to airworthy condition at Pattaya Air Park in 2007 and written off 20 December 2007; the wreck has been at the Tango Don Mueang museum since September 2011. Wears code 53155.
Probably ex USAF 56-2661; data plate missing. Stored at Prachuap Khiri Khan until 2008 and at the Tango Don Mueang museum since November 2008. Marked 53117 only.
c/n 22980 from the data plate. Ex Chiang Mai; flown from Pattaya on occasion up to 2006, then static in the Tango Don Mueang museum. Marked 53182.

Ex Royal Thai Army 50-1634, c/n 21326 from the data plate. Derelict at the Lopburi Maintenance Battalion in 2001, then at Tango Amphur Khaeng Koi and Saraburi Aero Park; first noted at Don Mueang January 2020.

Ex Royal Thai Army 51-12190, c/n 22504 from the data plate. Derelict at the Lopburi Maintenance Battalion in 2001, then at Tango Amphur Khaeng Koi and Saraburi Aero Park; first noted at Don Mueang January 2020.
Ex USAF 68-10818. In the 904 Squadron hangar at Don Mueang 1995-97 and static in the Tango Don Mueang museum from August 2002. Marked 21111.
Ex USAF 71-0802. Static in the Tango Don Mueang museum since August 2002. Marked 21123.
Ex G-AMOU from the data plate; exported to Thailand November 1993. Marked 21 and named Pimantip. At the Tango Don Mueang museum since June 2009.
c/n C1/0619. Ex Chiang Mai; at the Tango Don Mueang museum since August 2004.
c/n C1/0634. In the Tango Don Mueang hangar from October 1995 and static in the museum since August 2002. Marked 66.

Ex USAF 52-4463; reported in 1997-2001 as Korean Air Force 24-463. Static in the Tango Don Mueang museum since August 2002; repainted in false marks for a film in October 2012. Marked 5085 with code 1332.
Ex USAF 51-13345 (radio call 113345); reported in 1997-2001 as Korean Air Force 13-345. Static in the Tango Don Mueang museum since August 2002. Marked 5093 with code 1325.
Ex USAF 51-14662. Ex Chiang Mai; at the Tango Don Mueang museum since February 2004. Marked 1-14662 with code 5301.
Flying replica of the original Travel Air 2000 Miss Siam, the first aircraft privately owned in Siam; registered 27 December 2000 and moved to the Tango Don Mueang museum about October 2003.
Ex N99X c/n 948, bought in the USA about 1994 and restored at Chiang Mai; at the Tango Don Mueang museum since February 2004. Also carries Miss Siam titles.
Static exhibit built around the original fuselage frame of the Travel Air 2000 Miss Siam. In the Tango Don Mueang museum since August 2002.
c/n 15911; sold to Tango about 1993, at Chiang Mai until 2005 and at the Tango Don Mueang museum since 2009.
Wreck, c/n 0120; static in the Tango Don Mueang museum since August 2002.
Royal Thai Police 412EP wreck, noted at Don Mueang from January 2012 and moved into the Tango Don Mueang compound by January 2020.
Royal Thai Police 412EP wreck, noted at Don Mueang from February 2003 and moved into the Tango Don Mueang compound by January 2020. Serial not displayed.
